rejectedRestoringStudy.rejection: Strong K1173 tune gave downward equivalent assist near extension and both prescribed-height runs reached travel limits near1.98s. Of three upward-assist candidates, two ran the prescribed bench but none avoided terrain endstops. No restoring trial is saved as a final design. Exact final benchmark outcomes belong to the separate paired-engine report.

massBasis.wheelTreatment: With fixed world wheel height and zero contact moment, wheel gravity has zero stance work. Its weight remains in the ground reaction and in dynamic wheel mass/inertia. Moving link/compound gravity is included at each actual COM; alpha changes its world-height work.

fits.method: Bounded sampled minimax static holding-torque fit over the full95..175deg working range, with no post-fit ride-pose root. The initial135deg residual is retained, so zero-input drift is expected. Not a guaranteed global optimum, height controller or terrain stability guarantee.

limits: Supported-stance gravity compensation only. Both saved designs retain their actual nonzero135deg fit residual, zero initial velocity and upward spring-equivalent assist. No post-fit ride balancing is applied; initial downward drift is expected. Near-neutral support is not passive world-height regulation. Geometry-only trials did not solve the150mm terrain case without other failures; no hidden motor bias, damping or changes to k/preload are used. At alpha20 finite-link COM gravity makes the equivalent support target pose-dependent. Working stops are inset from the singular ideal90-degree endpoint. The app bench uses a stationary flat input; actual contact uses zero prescribed transition. Entered250/300Nm commands are illustrative ideal joint torques, not certified actuator capability. Actual outcomes, impact losses, packaging and strength require separate validation.
